The essential distinction

Energy tells you how much. Power tells you what is happening.

Seeing both gives facility teams a much clearer picture of consumption, loading and operating behavior.

kWh

Energy

Accumulated consumption

Energy is the total electricity used over time—the value typically associated with the utility bill.

Think of kWh like the total distance on a vehicle odometer.
kW

Power

Instantaneous demand

Power is the rate of electricity use right now. It helps reveal loading, peaks and sudden operational changes.

Think of kW like the speed shown on a speedometer.

Frequently asked questions

What teams want to know before monitoring.

What does MeterSight show?

MeterSight can display live power, energy, phase voltage, current, power factor, demand, frequency, harmonics, alarms and historical trends based on the installed meters.

Why does power factor matter?

Low power factor can increase current, consume system capacity and contribute to utility penalties. Monitoring helps identify when and where it occurs.

Can it help investigate nuisance trips or electrical faults?

Historical loading, voltage and event context can help teams narrow the investigation. It complements—rather than replaces—protective-device studies and field diagnostics.

What types of electrical systems can be monitored?

Projects may include single-phase, split-phase, three-phase and multi-circuit metering, depending on the selected hardware and application.

How often does the data update?

Screen refresh and historical logging intervals are configurable and depend on the connected meters, network and project requirements.

Can the system send alarms?

Yes. Alarm logic and delivery can be configured around items such as demand, voltage, power factor, imbalance and communications status.
